goals: Keep GrabAndGo 1.0.1 carried-entity rendering functional on Minecraft Java 26.2 by assigning safe identity to its otherwise unassigned client-created synthetic entities before render-state extraction.

Preserve the actual carried Ribbit and other supported entity models across first-person, third-person, shadow, GUI picture-in-picture, shader, and ordinary world renderer passes without suppressing rendering or changing real entity behavior.
Preserve full carried entity/container data across logout, restart and player replacement, synchronize restored state, and consume it only after successful logical-server restoration.
scope: Preserve Canary 2 render-only cache/ID behavior and Ribbit first/third-person translation values unchanged.

Common logical-server persistence accepts valid legacy STRING and COMPOUND and writes canonical COMPOUND without selecting fields; malformed tags and inconsistent occupied state remain durably preserved with deduplicated diagnostics.

Intercept only the two audited upstream player persistence callbacks and entity/block placement entry points. Restore complete entity/passenger NBT or off-world decoded block entities; reject missing IDs, UUID conflicts and decoding failures without default replacements; guard consumption, retries and partial side effects. Copy remaining carry state during ServerPlayer replacement.

Pin build/fixtures to public GrabAndGo maven.modrinth:199VyzmC:STumnqJf, mod ID grapandgo 1.0.1, 381703 bytes, SHA-256 9360863791c9e2f898de7abf5c2a671343fa47b793fadd51cc41bf254ef5bb64. Runtime dependency remains the stable provider >=1.0.1.

Package common persistence separately from client rendering; validate production Knot CLIENT and dedicated SERVER application, actual upstream callback/placement fixtures, NBT types, synchronization and existing renderer regressions.

exclusions: No GrabAndGo rewrite or bundled upstream code, no Ribbits payload changes, no cached render-entity spawning or synthetic-ID persistence, and no unrelated features.

No user-save modification, automatic recovery framework, or promise to recover data already lost without a retained payload/backup. Decoder rejection or uncertain partial effects retain the payload and block retries for inspected recovery.

No Test Instance Manager mutation/deployment or live Minecraft/server testing in this artifact task. Preserve occupied cohorts; the protected Matcha Flavoured 26.1.2 gameplay instance remains off-limits.
